claude.performance_metric: Equity earnings drag: increasing Sadara losses (affiliate equity earnings $1,034M→$835M→$674M, 2013-2015), incl. $27M Dow-share Epoxy Plant engineering write-off; first polyethylene production achieved Dec 2015
claude.rationale: The slice documents only a development-stage venture ramping toward operation, not a realized product/process interface disruption: the complex followed a sequenced multi-year start-up that "remain[ed] on schedule," achieving first polyethylene production in December 2015, so p4=0. No documented friction between operations and people/management/culture appears—reported outcomes are financial (rising equity losses, a $27M engineering write-off, continuing parent funding) and milestone-based, with nothing about organizational or workforce fracture, so p5=0. No evidence of controlling-intent archetype incoherence or business-model incompatibility is present within the window.

gemini.performance_metric: increased equity losses and $27m write-off (Dow's share)
gemini.rationale: The slice documents that Sadara remained a development-stage company with increased equity losses and a $27 million write-off for design engineering work. However, there is no documented evidence of product/process incoherence (p4_pathway) or process/organization fracture (p5_pathway) over time; the venture achieved its first production milestone on schedule.

grok.performance_metric: increased equity losses incl. $27M epoxy design write-off; still development-stage at ~3-4 yrs
grok.rationale: The slice documents Sadara remaining a development-stage equity-method affiliate through FY2015, with a sequenced start-up described as on schedule and first polyethylene production achieved in December 2015; the $27M (Dow share) write-off of epoxy-plant design engineering is a project cost item, not product/process interface incoherence, so p4_pathway=0. No evidence is given of operations-versus-organization, people, management, or culture fracture over the window, so p5_pathway=0.
